clue.text: Finished non-acting job in 5’s city

indicators.note: 'non-' negates the word it is fixed to, so that word's abbreviation must be taken away

blocks.note: a. is a dictionary abbreviation for acting; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone has wrapped up a job that involved no acting, somewhere in a Ukrainian city.
explanation.walkthrough: DONE then TASK without its A gives DONETSK. The '5' points to the answer at 5-across, UKRAINE, so the definition is a city in Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: Donetsk is a large industrial city in eastern Ukraine, the country found at 5-across.

clue.text: Neocon I routinely hosted upriver

indicators.note: to host is to have guests inside, so the letters sit within the words before it
in a down clue 'up' means read from bottom to top, the opposite way

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word to the start of the third
one printed word doing two jobs: its first two letters signal the reversal and the rest is the definition

explanation.surface: A neoconservative is routinely put up somewhere far up a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upriver' looks like one word of the surface, but it splits into the reversal signal 'up' and the definition 'river'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a major South American waterway flowing through Venezuela to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Small book label provided by former politician

blocks.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A little bookplate has been supplied by someone who used to be in politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' tells you the definition is in short form: ex libris, 'from the books of', is the Latin on a bookplate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex-lib is the shortened form of ex libris, the inscription on a bookplate marking the owner's library.

clue.text: Make content but Spooner’s plump men moan

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds here change places

blocks.note: plump men are fatties and to moan is to sigh; swap their opening F and S sounds

explanation.surface: Pleasing people is the aim, yet overweight men are grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: Fatties sigh becomes 'satties figh', which said aloud is SATISFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy someone is to please them, leaving them contented and happy with what they got.

clue.text: Country drops language finally – it uses Russian in places

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A nation abandons a language in the end, though it still speaks Russian in some areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like the definition, but it gives only UK; the definition is the whole last phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine's official tongue is Ukrainian, but Russian is still widely spoken in some eastern and southern regions.

clue.text: Briefly smack Kite – ultimately tempt fate

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped
ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter is wanted

blocks.note: a smack is a loud kiss
Kite is the setter, who refers to themselves

explanation.surface: A quick dare: give the setter a slap and see if you get away with it.
explanation.walkthrough: A smack is a loud kiss, not a blow. The setter's name in a clue stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is a Turkish-derived word meaning destiny, the predetermined course of a person's life.

clue.text: You, having sex noisily at first, regularly dress for poses

indicators.note: something done noisily is heard, so we want how the phrase sounds when spoken
at first means at the start, so this piece is placed before the one it is attached to
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: a couple having sex are 'at it', which runs together when said
U is the text-speak spelling of you
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Someone loudly having sex keeps changing outfits to strike poses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' places the sound of 'at it' before U.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitude is a bodily posture or stance, especially a striking one adopted for display, as in ballet.

clue.text: Silly people make pasta

blocks.note: second meaning: long strips of dough

explanation.surface: Fools are in the kitchen preparing a pasta dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' reads as cooking but is only a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is informal for a foolish person, and the plural also names strips of dough boiled and eaten.

clue.text: Box type of seats I’d made

definitions.note: the answer is the type of box rather than the box itself

indicators.note: made means constructed or put together, so the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: Someone is describing what sort of box seats they built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box type' looks like the definition, but 'type' belongs in the letters; 'Box' alone is the definition, standing for the kind of box named.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety deposit box is a locked container rented in a bank vault for storing valuables.

clue.text: Face becoming possibly relaxed

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: laid as in laid-back, at ease

explanation.surface: Someone's expression is turning calm and easy-going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' looks like 'attractive' but just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dial is slang for a person's face, from the round face of a clock or watch.

clue.text: Artist in on designs for move

indicators.note: designs are new arrangements, so the letters are laid out to a new plan

explanation.surface: A painter is working on plans for a house move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designs' reads as an artist's plans, but it signals the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A transition is a change or passage from one state, place or stage to another.

clue.text: Graduate puts on masks in European industrial region

indicators.note: a mask covers what lies behind it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A graduate dons a disguise in an industrial area of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masks' reads as a noun for disguises but is the verb doing the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Donbas is the coal and steel basin of eastern Ukraine, a heavily industrialised area.

clue.text: Best, retired clergyman half cut inside but capable of standing up

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word is read backwards
half means only part is kept, so the second half of the word is dropped
to cut inside is to push into the middle, so one piece is inserted in the other

explanation.surface: A retired priest, halfway drunk, still manages to stay on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half cut' is British slang for drunk, but here 'half' and 'cut inside' are separate instructions. ETILE takes REC after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Erectile describes tissue or structures able to become rigid and upright, as when engorged with blood.

clue.text: Every dozy monk slyly working for iconic leader

indicators.note: something working is in operation, its parts moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Each sleepy monk is quietly toiling on behalf of a revered religious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a monastery and its spiritual leader; the four Ys and the Z make the fodder easy to spot once the theme is clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Zelensky, president of Ukraine since 2019, became a globally recognised wartime figure after the Russian invasion.

clue.text: Song of the Deep depicting dolphins’ home?

definitions.note: singular in the clue, while the answer is the plural

blocks.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A film or song title is asked to show where dolphins live.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title reads as one thing, but 'Song of the Deep' is the instruction: the song belongs to the deep, so the sea comes first. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanaria are large seawater aquariums where marine creatures such as dolphins are kept on display.

clue.text: European has too much, drinking first of Andalusian port

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so one piece goes inside another
the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: someone who has too much ODs, overdoses

explanation.surface: A European overindulges, drinking in a Spanish harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Andalusian port' sounds like a Spanish town such as Cádiz, but only the A is used; 'port' alone is the definition. ODS swallows E, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Odesa is Ukraine's chief harbour city on the Black Sea, a major shipping hub.

clue.text: Son went to race

blocks.note: to go, informally, is to urinate

explanation.surface: A boy set off to take part in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' looks like travelled, but it is the informal sense of going to the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to move very fast, which is what speeding means.

clue.text: Table water follows dish in Paris

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so this piece is placed second
in Paris tells you to use the French words for the pieces

explanation.surface: At a Paris dinner table, water comes after the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' asks for French words, and 'follows' puts the water after the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a tableland, a raised area of fairly flat ground.

clue.text: See 14
Cook single hard tongue

indicators.note: to cook is to mix ingredients and transform them, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: H is the pencil grade for hard

explanation.surface: A recipe: prepare one tough ox tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' reads as meat for cooking, but it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue is an old word for a language, and English is the language of England.

clue.text: Comply with oily diet, not one processed

indicators.note: not one means without one, and one is the Roman numeral I, which is taken out
processed food has been treated and changed, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words, with one I removed

explanation.surface: Someone sticks to a greasy diet, avoiding any processed food.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a diet without processed food, but 'not one' removes an I and 'processed' scrambles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield to a demand is to give way and obey it, accepting its authority.

clue.text: Medic that is beginning to suture receives right desiccants

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
receiving takes something in, so one piece goes inside

explanation.surface: A doctor about to start stitching a wound is handed the correct drying agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' looks like 'correct' in the surface, but it is just the letter R slipped in near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiccants are substances that absorb moisture, so they act as drying agents.

clue.text: Philanthropic doctor coming from pub close to drug-free party

indicators.note: free of a drug means without it, and the drug ecstasy is E, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: near means close to; its E is dropped

explanation.surface: A charitable doctor leaves a pub near a party where no drugs are allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like a pointer to a last letter, but it is NEAR, which loses E for ecstasy. Thomas Barnardo founded homes for destitute children in Victorian London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Barnardo was a Victorian physician whose children's charity still bears his surname today.

clue.text: Try to write letters, almost providing the truth

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
to spell is to write the letters of a word

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to write correspondence in order to tell the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'write letters' suggests correspondence, but it means to spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel, as in 'take it as gospel', means something accepted as absolutely true.

clue.text: Serious, thus drink half-heartedly

indicators.note: the heart is the middle, so half of the central pair of letters goes

blocks.note: beer is a drink; one of its middle Es goes

explanation.surface: Being solemn, someone sips their drink without enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' reads as lacking enthusiasm, but it removes one of the two central letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober can mean grave and earnest in manner, not frivolous or playful.

clue.text: End of union residence I abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A marriage breaks up when someone walks out of the family home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' fits the story of leaving home, but signals rearrangement. In English law a decree nisi was the provisional divorce order.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree nisi is the court order beginning the dissolution of a marriage, the first step to divorce.

clue.text: Natural defender not against organisation

indicators.note: not means without, so the following word's letters are taken away

blocks.note: antibodies are the immune system's own defence
anti means against; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A champion of nature who supports, rather than opposes, an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural defender' sounds like an environmentalist but is the immune system's protein.
explanation.definitionFit: A body is an organised group such as a governing body or a professional association.

clue.text: One in the 12 getting rare metal German kitchen top

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across clue is its opening letter

blocks.note: Lu is the symbol for lutetium, a rare earth metal
Hans is a typical German name

explanation.surface: Someone in a group of twelve acquires a precious metal German worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 12' refers to the answer at 12-across, DONBAS, the region containing this city.
explanation.definitionFit: Luhansk is a city and province in the Donbas, alongside Donetsk in eastern Ukraine.

clue.text: King (and Queen’s descendant?) in 5’s place

explanation.surface: A king, perhaps a queen's son too, is somewhere in Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that HER SON is a cheeky way to read a queen's descendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Kherson is a port city on the Dnipro river in southern Ukraine, the country at 5-across.
